Text: What Was Reviewed | ・ | Application-oriented quantum benchmarking studies | • Transport-problem instances examined in quantum studies | • Reported circuit widths and resource estimates | • Formulations and encodings used to construct the circuits | • Evaluation modalities supporting the reported results Similar application-instance scales may lead to different circuit widths. | What Was Observed | • Circuit width depends on problem instance, formulation, and |  encoding. | • Similar problem-instance scales may lead to different circuit widths depending on formulation and encoding. | • Reported qubit counts must be interpreted together with the problem instance, formulation, encoding, and evaluation modality. | • Executing a wide circuit does not, by itself, establish quantum  utility. | • Application-side requirements must be defined before resource  requirements can be interpreted. | Survey: What Was Checked and What Was Learned | Reviewed how transport problems are translated into reported circuit widths and how those values are supported through simulation, hardware execution, or resource estimation.
